Author: FLYBYME <mangoraft@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Sep 8 15:20:03 2026 -0400

    One published API shape for every part; internal becomes mandatory
    
    Phase 1a of the rebuild: the contract types. src/ typechecks clean; the 62
    test errors are the intended breakage and are the next commit.
    
    NEW src/contribution/api.ts
    
      PartApi        commands, components, state - the same three slots for every
                     part, so a consumer knows where to look without knowing which
                     part it holds. state is ReadonlySignal, never Signal: read is
                     an observable value, write is a command.
      CommandContract  action, description, input, output, available(), confirm.
                     available() lives ON the command - PeopleApi kept five
                     *Availability() methods parallel to five commands, synced by
                     hand. Folded in, a command cannot exist without an
                     availability answer.
      Component/CompositeContract  a component has no logic, a composite has state.
                     The twelve orphaned form buffers in PeopleApi are the proof
                     the distinction is real: they exist, they belong somewhere,
                     and "composite" is the somewhere.
      Schema<T>      a phantom type plus optional JSON Schema. NOT zod. This
                     package has no runtime dependencies and net/api.ts already
                     settled this exact problem with a phantom `types?` member.
      checkBindings  refuses a part whose declared command has no implementation,
                     and one that binds something undeclared. A declaration
                     nothing implements is worse than an absent one: it advertises.
    
    CHANGED
    
      ApplicationStartResult was a three-branch conditional whose stated job was
      "preserving complete backwards compatibility" with parts that never opted
      into the public/private split. It is now ApplicationInstance. ClockApp's
      five type parameters become three.
    
      internal is mandatory. The default of `never` is what produced every
      over-published API here: opting out was free, so render received the public
      API, so everything a view touched became public - ending at
      newAccountPassword: Signal<string>, publicly writable.
    
      ViewContext/ViewDecl reordered to params, internal, app - input, state,
      output. A view reads internal; reaching for app to find its own state is the
      mistake the ordering makes obvious.
    
      Declarations.publishes is the static half, readable before anything runs.
      Named publishes because `api` is already the inward surface - the API a part
      talks to. The two point opposite ways.
    
      IntentActor: 'user' | 'agent' | 'part' on the description layer. RULES 7
      requires every destructive write to confirm, and a confirmation is a control
      that answers an intent - so something that can raise commit defeats the check
      protecting cdn.deploy, release_repo and every delete. Same bug as this
      morning's tenant leak, one layer up: absence is never a safe signal.

ce — see ApplicationInstance.`

nd makes `start()` require `Promise<ApplicationStartResult<ApiOf<TProvides>, never>>`, rejecting any implementation returning `{ internal: {} }` or `{ internal: state }` because `{}` cannot be assigned to
